question.text: Under Section 23A of SCRA, if a listed company fails to furnish required information to the stock exchange and the failure continues for 80 days, what is the maximum penalty that can be imposed?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 23A of SCRA, the penalty may extend to Rs. 1 lakh for each day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1 crore for each failure. For a failure lasting 80 days, the per-day calculation gives Rs. 1 lakh x 80 = Rs. 80 lakh, which is below the Rs. 1 crore cap. The maximum penalty that can be imposed in this scenario is therefore Rs. 80 lakh. The Trap: The Rs. 1 crore figure is the statutory cap on the per-failure penalty, not a flat amount that can be imposed regardless of duration. The cap only bites when the per-day calculation, accumulated over the failure period, reaches or exceeds Rs. 1 crore - which would require the failure to continue for 100 days or more. Note: Always work the per-day amount first (Rs. 1 lakh x number of days of failure) and only apply the Rs. 1 crore cap when that calculation exceeds it.
